title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 27–29). A 'figure' F is an admissible finite set of closed sub-varieties X of an ambient space E, ordered by inclusion. Each X has an 'open stratum' X° = X minus the members of F strictly below it. |F| is the union of the members, stratified by these X°. Page 27 shows that a saturated (down-closed) subset F' of the poset F is again a figure, called a sub-figure, written F' ≤ F. It also warns that a subset F' ⊂ F that is itself a figure need not be a sub-figure.

Page 28 defines when two figures F and G are compatible. First comes a 'set-theoretic' (ensembliste) notion, with several conditions claimed equivalent:
(a) |F| ∩ |G| is a saturated part (a union of strata) of both |F| and |G|, and the two induced stratifications (equivalence relations) on it coincide.
(b) For every stratum U = X° of F and V = Y° of G, either U ∩ V = ∅ or U = V. (b') is the same statement as X° ∩ Y° = ∅ or X = Y.
(c) For all X ∈ F and Y ∈ G, X ∩ Y is saturated in |F| and in |G|.
(d) F ∪ G is admissible, and F and G are saturated subsets of it.
In short, the two stratifications agree on their overlap.

Consequences listed:
- F ∩ G is closed (down-closed) in F and in G.
- F and G are closed in F ∪ G.
- As an ordered set, F ∪ G is the amalgamated sum (poset pushout) F ⊔_{F∩G} G.

The full definition then reads: F and G are compatible if they are set-theoretically compatible, F ∪ G is a figure, and F and G are sub-figures of F ∪ G. Example: two sub-figures of a common figure H are compatible, because F ∪ G is a down-closed subset of H, hence a sub-figure and so a figure.

Finally, a 'configuration' is a set of figures that are pairwise compatible. The next page conjectures (Conj. 4) that compatibility can be tested on 'multiplets'. It also deduces that a finite configuration has a union that is a figure containing every member as a sub-figure.

Purpose: this is a combinatorial/poset foundation for a 'tame' analysis situs. Stratified objects are glued along common closed sub-stratifications; this is the groundwork for describing tame spaces by finite stratified data, as envisaged in Esquisse d'un programme §5.
errors: The equivalence (a)⇔(b)⇔(c)⇔(d) is asserted, not proved. In particular, deriving (b) from (c) requires that strata be recovered from the closures X via saturation; that holds under the admissibility hypotheses of the earlier pages but is not shown here.

The poset-pushout claim F ∪ G = F ⊔_{F∩G} G is correct. Given down-closedness, any inclusion X ⊂ Y with X ∈ F \ G and Y ∈ G would force X ∈ G, so no new order relations appear across the two pieces. This is left implicit.
Pairwise compatibility implies that the union is a figure only for finite families. The next page restricts to finite I, so nothing is wrong, but the page itself does not state the restriction.

ideas.what: Compatibility of two stratifications: strata pairwise disjoint or equal; the intersection is a union of strata in both
ideas.modern_name: compatible stratifications / stratifications agreeing on overlaps; gluing of stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather, Łojasiewicz (1960s); o-minimal cell decomposition, van den Dries (1980s–90s)
ideas.where_published: Spirit only: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (tame topology, dévissage of stratified structures). The precise definition is unpublished.

ideas.what: The union of compatible figures is the amalgamated sum of posets along the common down-closed subset
ideas.modern_name: pushout of posets along sieves; gluing poset-stratified spaces along closed unions of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cf. poset-stratified spaces (Lurie, Higher Algebra, Appendix A)

ideas.what: A configuration is a family of pairwise compatible figures
ideas.modern_name: a compatible system of stratified subspaces (a family admitting a common stratification)

missed.claim: This page and its neighbours are part of a systematic, purely combinatorial axiomatization of tame analysis situs (figures, sub-figures, compatibility, configurations, and a locality conjecture for compatibility on the next page). It is a concrete written trace of the 1984 Esquisse tame-topology programme, but the content of this page is routine definitional groundwork.
missed.quote: Configuration : ensemble de figures deux à deux compatibles.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical interest only. It documents how Grothendieck intended to found tame topology on finite posets of sub-varieties, close in spirit to poset-stratified spaces and exit-path categories.

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard definitions: compatibility of stratifications and gluing along common closed sub-stratifications. They are carefully stated and of historical interest as part of the unpublished Analysis situs programme, but contain nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: The word written above the struck-out 'mutuellement' is very likely 'ensemblistement', not '𝒱'. Read: On dit alors que F et G sont "ensemblistement compatibles".
Likely reading of the full definition: 'On dit que F et G sont compatibles, s'ils le sont ensemblistement, si F ∪ G est une figure, et si F, G sont des sous-figures de F ∪ G.'
Example line likely reads: 'Ex: Si F et G sont des sous-figures d'une figure H, alors ils le sont ensemblistement, et sont compatibles (car F ∪ G est une sous-figure de H, donc une figure).'
In (c) the parenthetical likely reads '(équivalent à la saturation pour les stratifications des variétés X, Y)'. The struck-out word in (d) is 'fermés', replaced by 'saturés'.
(a) continues: 'et les deux rel. d'équiv. [induites] coïncident'.
